elements.name: route_intro
elements.html:
What happens after Send?

In a typical cloud chat app, your app sends a request over the network, usually using encrypted HTTPS. A server receives it and prepares the conversation for a model.

The model processes tokens (pieces of text) and generates output step by step using learned patterns. That is inference. The service sends the reply back through the network to your app, often a piece at a time.

This is a simplified route: services may add safety checks or tools. Sending “hi” does not necessarily retrain the model immediately; later use of chats depends on the service’s policies and settings.

elements.name: route
elements.title: Which route best describes this cloud chat?

choices.text: App → model inside every phone → answer
App → network → server → model inference → reply back
App → search engine → copied answer every time

elements.name: route_right
elements.html: Yes. The app is the interface; a remote service runs inference and returns the output. Some apps use on-device models, but that is a different setup.

elements.name: route_retry
elements.html: Try again if you like. For this cloud example, the request travels to a server. A model can generate a reply without searching the web. The route above shows the missing steps.

elements.name: claim_intro
elements.html:
A reply lands in your group chat.

Fictional AI answer

“Every message sent to an AI instantly trains it. That means the more confidently it answers, the more accurate it must be.”

You are about to share this with your class. What do you do first?

choices.text: Share it — the explanation sounds confident.
Ask the same AI whether it is sure.
Check reliable sources and the service’s documentation.

elements.name: share_feedback
elements.html: Pause before sharing. A confident tone is a style of output, not a measure of truth. Follow the evidence path on the next screen.

elements.name: ask_feedback
elements.html: A second answer can help clarify the claim, but the same model may repeat its mistake. Follow the evidence path next.

elements.name: verify_feedback
elements.html: Good move. Check what a source actually says, who published it, and whether it applies to this service.

elements.name: detour_intro
elements.html:
What would make the claim checkable?

Repeating a claim can make it familiar without making it true. Find evidence outside the original answer.

choices.text: Another confident answer from the same chat.
Documentation that distinguishes training from inference, plus the service’s data-use policy.

elements.name: detour_feedback
elements.html: Look for documentation and a policy that applies to the actual service. Repetition alone is not independent support.

elements.name: evidence_cards
elements.html:
Inspect the evidence

These are fictional practice cards, not quotations from a real provider.

Card A · Model documentation

Training adjusts model parameters using data. Inference uses a trained model to produce outputs. Generating an answer does not itself mean the model’s parameters changed.

Card B · Example service policy

Conversation data may be used in later improvement processes, depending on settings and policy. This does not mean every message instantly retrains the model.

choices.text: The original claim is supported in full.
No service ever uses conversations for training.
The claim overstates things: inference differs from training, policies vary, and confidence does not prove accuracy.

elements.name: verdict_good
elements.html: Exactly. You separated how a model responds from how a service might later use data. The confident wording was not evidence.

elements.name: verdict_bad
elements.html: Revisit the cards. They do not support “every message instantly trains it” or “no service ever uses chats.” A careful conclusion keeps the policy-dependent detail.

elements.name: reflection_intro
elements.html:
Write the message you would send instead.

In one or two sentences, explain why the original claim needs correcting and name one check you would make before sharing it. Use practice text only; no names or personal information.

validators.text: Add a little more reasoning (at least 20 characters).

elements.name: rubric
elements.html:
Self-check: Did you distinguish inference from training? Mention policies or settings? Explain why evidence beats confidence?

Your writing is saved on this device only. It is not AI graded; completion means you submitted a reflection, not that a teacher assessed it.
